page: Amazon Web Services r7a.medium is a memory-optimized virtual server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features a single dedicated physical core and vCPU from an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 4 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core. There is no bundled local storage or GPU hardware.

Benchmark results show strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%. However, due to its single-core configuration, multi-core CPU and multi-threaded performance metrics are weak, falling into the bottom 25% or bottom 10% across Geekbench and Passmark suites. Memory bandwidth for cached small blocks is poor, though large block write bandwidth remains average. Cryptographic and compression tasks, such as single-threaded gzip and bzip3 operations, perform at average levels, while database operations and static web serving throughput are relatively low.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r7a.medium offers a low-cost entry point into the DDR5 memory-optimized class without requiring the commitment of multi-core instances. It is best suited for memory-bound, single-threaded workloads, lightweight database caching, basic text processing, or small-scale development and testing environments that require dedicated CPU execution but do not demand high multi-threaded throughput or local storage.
